title: ADAR3 modulates neuronal differentiation and regulates mRNA stability and translation
projectDescription: This study aims to elucidate potential functions of the editing-deficient ADAR3 enzyme in Mouse. This dataset aims to investigate the binding partners of the ADAR3 enzyme, both with and without RNAse treatment in order to differentiate between RNA dependent and independent interactions. The control is a Co-IP of a FLAG-tagged Luciferase protein.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells were harvested in lysis buffer (20 mM Tris pH 8.0, 300 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 1% Triton x-100) and centrifuged for 30 min at 17500g. Lysates were incubated with 100ug/ml RNAse A for 30 min at RT followed by Control Agarose Resin for 30 minutes. Samples were then transferred to magnetic anti-flag M2 beads for 4 hours at 4 degrees. The beads were washed 5 times in Lysis buffer (2% triton x-100) followed by 5 washes in lysis buffer without triton. Elution was performed with 300ng/ul FLAG-peptide for 2 hours at 4 degrees. Peptides from N2a cells and the ADAR3 co-IP were analyzed by LC-MS on a fusion or an Eclipse tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific), respectively and operated in the positive data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data was processed by Proteome Discoverer version 2.5 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and peptides were identified using SEQUEST HT against UniProtKB mouse database (UP000000589 plus isoforms).
